The dovish condition this brief set on 4 September has failed outright: 3.4% against a 3.0% test, moving up rather than down. Oil eased for the first time in a week, WTI −3.35% to $99.05. items.html: BAC — The thesis got exactly the environment it asked for. August CPI printed in line at +3.4% year over year with core a tenth hot at +0.3% on the month, and the bond market took it as permission: Treasury yields set fresh 52-week highs across the curve, the ten-year at 4.959%, and odds of a hike on Wednesday jumped to 85.6% from roughly 70% the day before. Filed as a signal because this is the cleanest test the position will get — higher-for-longer is no longer a forecast, it is 86% priced. Thursday's mark had it at −0.46R. If a bank cannot make money from this setup, the thesis is the problem rather than the timing.

world.title: An in-line print that hardened the Fed, oil back under $100, and a week with two events in it.

items.html: August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year, both matching consensus; core rose 0.3%, a tenth above forecast, and 2.4% annually. Equities read it as relief and broke a four-day losing streak; the bond market read it as a green light and set fresh 52-week highs across the curve, the ten-year at 4.959%. Odds of a hike on Wednesday: 85.6%. When two markets disagree this sharply about one number, the bond market is usually the one to believe.

WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70, the first decline in a week and back below $100. That eases the mechanism feeding the CPI gate — but from $102, after a month in which crude added nearly a quarter, and with Saudi production reported at its lowest since 1990. One down day does not undo a supply story.

The FOMC meets Tuesday and Wednesday and decides on the 16th with a hike 85.6% priced. The Bank of Japan meets this week with a hike 97% priced. Triple witching is Friday the 18th. All three land into a dealer position that is still deeply short gamma. A decision that is 86% priced has an asymmetric surprise: the damage is in a hold, not a hike.

stance.title: Reinforced, not merely unchanged — Friday removed the argument against it.

macro.title: The front end is finally moving, and the long end is at levels it has not seen since 2007.

items.html: Phoenix has the ten-year at 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week and +26bp on the month; the two-year at 4.43%; the 2s10s curve at 51bp, steepened 5bp over the month; the real ten-year at 2.46%. Friday took the ten-year to 4.959% and set 52-week highs across the whole curve (TheStreet). The front end moving with the long end is the market repricing the policy path, not just term premium — which is what an 86% hike probability looks like in the curve.

The ten-year series now tracks daily. us02, real10 and hy still do not — all three read 0bp on the day for a fifth session — and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change between packs, which looks held rather than refreshed. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week — a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, on a record ¥360tn of cross-border borrowing, with the Bank of Japan meeting this week and a hike 97% priced. Two central banks tightening in the same week is the setup that turns a carry unwind disorderly.

High yield at 271bp once the unit switch is undone — inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful, and it has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries. Credit is not worried about a hike, which is the most reassuring number in this brief.

Phoenix has WTI at 102.48, +23.17% on the month. Friday reversed some of it: WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70 (TheStreet), back under $100. Gold is down 1.17% at 4,364.50 and bitcoin flat. Crude easing takes the first pressure off the inflation gate in a week — but it eased from $102, not from $80, with Saudi production at its lowest since 1990.

August CPI landed in line and the market hardened rather than relaxed. Headline +0.4%% on the month and +3.4%% on the year, both as expected; core +0.3%%, a tenth above forecast, and +2.4%% annually. Odds of a hike on 16 September went to 85.6%% from roughly 70%% on Thursday and a coin flip a week ago. The data and the Fed have stopped disagreeing entirely.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8 on Phoenix's figure, and Friday's 3.4 print widens that further; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp clears by 8bp; drawdown clears by 9.51. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

weekly.headline: The week the Fed stopped arguing with itself — and Palantir walked to its stop
weekly.standfirst: Four sessions, because Monday was Labor Day, and the index gave up about 0.6% across them — the third week running in which a great deal happened and the S&P barely moved. Underneath: crude through $100 on Saudi production at its lowest since 1990, the ten-year up 15bp to 4.94% with the thirty-year at levels last seen in June 2007, the VIX out of a 28-session range, and dealer gamma collapsing to −$44B before recovering. CPI then printed 3.4% in line on Friday and put a September hike at 85.6%, killing the dovish case this brief had been testing since 4 September. In the book AAPL turned green on a doubled revenue estimate and PLTR ended the week 0.75% above its stop after a Citigroup downgrade — whether it held is the open question of the weekend. Heat 3.15R against 3.0R.

AAPL led at +2.06%, PLTR lagged at -4.86% — and neither is the story

PLTRentered 2026-08-27 at 184.45 · stop 164.45-0.93R-4.86%-10.08%
AAPLentered 2026-08-28 at 321.96 · stop 301.99+0.23R+2.06%+1.43%

3 positions open into the weekend at 3.15R of heat against a 3.0R cap. The figure is recomputed per account: the pack reports 7.19R because _pk_portfolio sums both books and divides by one account's capital, which is the bug Gabriel caught on 9 September. Columns are the week to 2026-09-10 and entry-to-date; marks are Thursday's close because Friday is not yet in the engine.

The week's real event is a level, not a return. PLTR closed Thursday at 165.86, 0.85% above its stop, after Citigroup cut it to Market Perform on a P/E near 142 and BTIG went Neutral. Friday's close is not in Phoenix and I could not source one, so whether that stop held is the open question of the weekend. The Nasdaq rose 0.88% on the day, which makes a stop-out the less likely outcome — but 0.85% is inside this stock's ordinary intraday range, and if it has gone, heat falls to roughly 2.15R without a decision being made.

A Fed that stopped arguing with itself, and a stock that walked to its stop

1. The inflation question closed. CPI printed 3.4%% year over year against the 3.0%% test this brief had set as the first argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING — and it moved up from 3.3, not down. Odds of a hike at the 16 September meeting went from a coin flip a week earlier, to roughly 70%% on Thursday, to 85.6%% after the print. The regime's binding gate now clears its threshold by 0.9. There is no dovish case left to argue.

2. Dealer gamma collapsed and then partly recovered. Net gamma went −$3.98B on Tuesday, −$26.05B on Wednesday, −$44.19B on Thursday and −$37.62B in the latest pack. The index lost its 50-day on Thursday for the first time in this run. Friday's 1.06% rally on an in-line print is what that positioning does to ordinary news — and the same multiplier is pointed at Wednesday's decision. Phoenix's own diff never flagged any of it, because it tests for a sign flip and the sign was already negative.

3. Two positions resolved in opposite directions. AAPL launched the iPhone Duo at $1,999 — under the $2,000-plus that had been trailed — shipping 23 October, and the stock shrugged until Deepwater doubled its estimate of the Duo's share of fiscal 2027 iPhone revenue from 5%% to 10%%, sending it up 3.56%% and turning the position green. PLTR went the other way on a Citigroup downgrade, closing the week on its stop. Both were sell-side opinions rather than company news, which is worth noting: the book's two biggest moves this week came from analysts, not from the businesses.

4. Alphabet acquired a court. A US appeals court cleared 2,400–3,000-plus youth-addiction suits against Google, Meta, Snapchat and TikTok to proceed, and refused to delay the trial brought by 29 state attorneys general. That is materially larger than the FTC's YouTube probe this brief had been tracking, which remains unfiled after sixteen days. GOOG fell 2.09%% on the ruling and still finished the week as the book's steadiest name.

Oil stopped being a risk premium and became a supply number

WTI settled above $102 on Thursday and Brent reached $107.63, both through $100 for the first time since May, before Friday took WTI back to $99.05. The move was not a headline premium: Saudi Arabia reported production at its lowest level since 1990 after Houthi strikes on energy facilities including the 400,000 barrel-a-day Jazan refinery, and roughly ten commodity ships a day are crossing the Strait of Hormuz against a chokepoint that carries a fifth of world oil in peacetime. US petrol averaged $4.27 and diesel set a record.

The transmission into this book runs crude → CPI → the regime gate, and it worked all week. It also showed up somewhere more concrete: seven of the eight names in Phoenix's screener are now oil or marine shipping — DK, PBR, BP and PSX alongside BWLP, DAC and NMM. The war has stopped being a macro input and become what the screener returns. None of it is actionable while heat is over cap, and the screener has still reached nothing at its 20-bar horizon, so the verdict remains INSUFFICIENT.

Friday's 3.35%% fall in crude is the first thing to challenge that in two weeks. One down day from $102 is not a supply story ending.

Two central banks and an expiry, into a market that magnifies all three

FOMCFederal Reserve decision — a hike is 85.6% pricedWed2026-09-16
BOJBank of Japan decision — a hike is 97% pricedthis week2026-09-18
OPEXTriple witching — quarterly expiryFri2026-09-18

The Fed is the week. With a hike 85.6% priced the surprise is asymmetric: a hike is already in the price and a hold is not, so the larger move comes from the outcome nobody is positioned for — amplified by a dealer book still short gamma by $37.6B.

The Bank of Japan is the one that could hurt this book without any position being wrong. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week and a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, with a hike 97% priced on a record ¥360tn of cross-border yen borrowing. Two central banks tightening in the same week, into negative gamma and a quarterly expiry, is the combination that turns an orderly repricing into a disorderly one.

Three things to check first on Monday. Whether PLTR's stop held on Friday; whether credit still refuses to worry — high yield has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries, which is the most reassuring number anywhere in this brief; and whether heat is back under the cap, by a stop or by a decision.

items.html: Policy Tightening, week 2. The binding gate is CPI against a 2.5 threshold. Friday's print at 3.4% widened the cushion rather than narrowing it, and with a hike 85.6% priced for Wednesday the regime is not in question this week. The only open question is what the Fed does inside it.

Net gamma −$37.62B at Thursday's close, still deeply negative though off the −$44.19B low. Friday's 1.06% rally on an in-line print is exactly the exaggerated move this section has been warning about — and the same mechanism is pointed at Wednesday's decision.

Add no risk while heat is over cap. 4.04R against 3.0R including the managed GOOG position, 3.04R without it. Unchanged — and with the FOMC on Wednesday and triple witching on Friday, this is the worst week of the month to be carrying more risk than the rules allow.

stance.note: Two weeks held, and the case for it is stronger this morning than at any point since it was set.

markets.title: Friday's rally was a short-gamma move, and the engine has not priced it yet.

items.html: Press figures: the S&P rose 1.06%, the Dow 1.15%, the Nasdaq 0.88% and the Russell 1.04%, breaking a four-day losing streak. Treasury yields set fresh 52-week highs across the curve with the ten-year at 4.959%. Equities and bonds read the same print in opposite directions, and it is the bond market that put Wednesday at 85.6%.

Phoenix's figures below are Thursday's close; the scheduled run fires before the US open, so Friday is not in it. SPX 7,591.70, -0.58% on that day, -0.16% against the 50-day — below it — and +6.07% above the 200-day. VIX 17.26.

Net gamma −$37.62B, regime negative, distance to flip +1.04%. Off the −$44.19B extreme but still deeply reflexive. A 1% index rally on an in-line inflation print is what negative gamma looks like from the upside, and the multiplier is still there for Wednesday.
Flip level, call wall and put wall still null, so none of this pins to a price. market.dxy, us10y, gold and wti still null while the macro block carries all four.

markets.note: The risk sentence for the week: a Fed decision and triple witching land in the same five sessions, into a dealer position that magnifies whatever they produce.

macro.title: The front end is finally moving, and the long end is at levels it has not seen since 2007.

items.html: Phoenix has the ten-year at 4.94%, +11bp on the day, +15bp on the week and +26bp on the month; the two-year at 4.43%; the 2s10s curve at 51bp, steepened 5bp over the month; the real ten-year at 2.46%. Friday took the ten-year to 4.959% and set 52-week highs across the whole curve (TheStreet). The front end moving with the long end is the market repricing the policy path, not just term premium — which is what an 86% hike probability looks like in the curve.

The ten-year series now tracks daily. us02, real10 and hy still do not — all three read 0bp on the day for a fifth session — and hy is still quoted in percent rather than basis points. Bitcoin is also carrying an identical level and change between packs, which looks held rather than refreshed. Read the front end and credit at weekly resolution.

The dollar index is 99.09, +0.32% on the day and -0.47% on the week. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week — a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, on a record ¥360tn of cross-border borrowing, with the Bank of Japan meeting this week and a hike 97% priced. Two central banks tightening in the same week is the setup that turns a carry unwind disorderly.

High yield at 271bp once the unit switch is undone — inside the 300bp line that separates calm from watchful, and it has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries. Credit is not worried about a hike, which is the most reassuring number in this brief.

Phoenix has WTI at 102.48, +23.17% on the month. Friday reversed some of it: WTI fell 3.35% to $99.05 and Brent 3.61% to $103.70 (TheStreet), back under $100. Gold is down 1.17% at 4,364.50 and bitcoin flat. Crude easing takes the first pressure off the inflation gate in a week — but it eased from $102, not from $80, with Saudi production at its lowest since 1990.

August CPI landed in line and the market hardened rather than relaxed. Headline +0.4%% on the month and +3.4%% on the year, both as expected; core +0.3%%, a tenth above forecast, and +2.4%% annually. Odds of a hike on 16 September went to 85.6%% from roughly 70%% on Thursday and a coin flip a week ago. The data and the Fed have stopped disagreeing entirely.

macro.note: The gates. Three of four hold. CPI y/y at 3.3 clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.8 on Phoenix's figure, and Friday's 3.4 print widens that further; the real ten-year's three-month change at 33bp clears by 8bp; drawdown clears by 9.51. The two-year's three-month change at 29bp against 40bp still fails, though Friday's move argues it will not for long. Runner-up is ENERGY_GRIND, one gate short: it needs the three-month CPI change above 0.3 and sits at −0.16.

changed.title: The dovish case is gone, and the diff still cannot see a position walking up to its stop.

items.html: August CPI at or below 3.0%% — FAILED, and in the wrong direction. It printed 3.4%% against 3.3 previously, so the binding gate now clears its 2.5 threshold by 0.9 rather than 0.8. This was set on 4 September as the first real argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING; there is no such argument left, and Wednesday is 85.6%% priced.

PLTR closes below its stop — unresolved. It ended Thursday 0.75% above, and Friday is not in the engine. The Nasdaq's 0.88% gain makes a stop-out the less likely outcome, but this is an open question rather than a negative answer.
BoJ hikes and USDJPY below 150 — not met. The yen was 153.57 at Thursday's close, -4.13% on the week, and the Bank of Japan meets this week with a hike 97% priced.

invalidation.title: The Fed on Wednesday is the whole week.

items.html: The FOMC holds on Wednesday instead of hiking. A hike is 85.6% priced, so the surprise is asymmetric — a hike is in the price and a hold is not. In a market short gamma by $37.6B, a hold produces a larger rally than the news deserves, and would be the first genuine challenge to POLICY_TIGHTENING since the regime was set.

PLTR closes below 164.62. It was 0.75% away at Thursday's close and Friday is unpriced. If it has gone, heat falls from 4.04R to about 3.04R without a decision being made; if it has not, the position is sitting on its line into an FOMC week that ends in triple witching.

The Bank of Japan hikes this week and USDJPY breaks below 150. It is 153.57, -4.13% on the week, 97% priced, on a record ¥360tn cross-border carry position. Two central banks moving in one week, into negative gamma and triple witching, is what turns a repricing into a disorderly one.

weekly.headline: The week the Fed stopped arguing with itself — and Palantir walked to its stop
weekly.standfirst: Four sessions, because Monday was Labor Day, and the index gave up about 0.6% across them — the third week running in which a great deal happened and the S&P barely moved. Underneath: crude through $100 on Saudi production at its lowest since 1990, the ten-year up 15bp to 4.94% with the thirty-year at levels last seen in June 2007, the VIX out of a 28-session range, and dealer gamma collapsing to −$44B before recovering. CPI then printed 3.4% in line on Friday and put a September hike at 85.6%, killing the dovish case this brief had been testing since 4 September. In the book AAPL turned green on a doubled revenue estimate and PLTR ended the week 0.75% above its stop after a Citigroup downgrade — whether it held is the open question of the weekend. Heat 4.04R against 3.0R.

Four sessions, because Monday was Labor Day. Phoenix's week runs 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-10: the S&P fell -1.64%, the Nasdaq -1.60%, the Dow -2.53% and the Russell -2.85%. The VIX rose +22.78% to 17.84, breaking a 28-session range. WTI added +12.02% to 102.48, through $100 for the first time since May. The ten-year rose 15bp to 4.94%, the thirty-year reached its highest since June 2007, and mortgages crossed 7%. Gold -1.47%, the dollar -0.07%.

Friday is not in these figures. The engine's scheduled run fires before the US open, so 11 September is not yet priced. From the press: August CPI printed +0.4%% on the month and +3.4%% on the year, both in line, core a tenth hot at +0.3%%; equities broke a four-day losing streak with the S&P up 1.06%%, the Dow 1.15%% and the Nasdaq 0.88%%; Treasury yields set fresh 52-week highs across the curve, the ten-year at 4.959%%; and WTI fell 3.35%% to $99.05. Including Friday, the S&P finished the week down roughly 0.6%% — the third week running that a great deal happened and the index barely moved. (TheStreet, Yahoo Finance)

AAPL led at +2.06%, PLTR lagged at -4.86% — and neither is the story

4 positions open into the weekend at 4.04R of heat against a 3.0R cap, or 3.04R excluding the managed GOOG position the validator says to exclude. The figure is recomputed per account: the pack reports 7.19R because _pk_portfolio sums both books and divides by one account's capital, which is the bug Gabriel caught on 9 September. Columns are the week to 2026-09-10 and entry-to-date; marks are Thursday's close because Friday is not yet in the engine.

The week's real event is a level, not a return. PLTR closed Thursday at 165.86, 0.75% above its stop, after Citigroup cut it to Market Perform on a P/E near 142 and BTIG went Neutral. Friday's close is not in Phoenix and I could not source one, so whether that stop held is the open question of the weekend. The Nasdaq rose 0.88% on the day, which makes a stop-out the less likely outcome — but 0.75% is inside this stock's ordinary intraday range, and if it has gone, heat falls to roughly 3.04R without a decision being made.

A Fed that stopped arguing with itself, and a stock that walked to its stop

1. The inflation question closed. CPI printed 3.4%% year over year against the 3.0%% test this brief had set as the first argument against POLICY_TIGHTENING — and it moved up from 3.3, not down. Odds of a hike at the 16 September meeting went from a coin flip a week earlier, to roughly 70%% on Thursday, to 85.6%% after the print. The regime's binding gate now clears its threshold by 0.9. There is no dovish case left to argue.

2. Dealer gamma collapsed and then partly recovered. Net gamma went −$3.98B on Tuesday, −$26.05B on Wednesday, −$44.19B on Thursday and −$37.62B in the latest pack. The index lost its 50-day on Thursday for the first time in this run. Friday's 1.06% rally on an in-line print is what that positioning does to ordinary news — and the same multiplier is pointed at Wednesday's decision. Phoenix's own diff never flagged any of it, because it tests for a sign flip and the sign was already negative.

3. Two positions resolved in opposite directions. AAPL launched the iPhone Duo at $1,999 — under the $2,000-plus that had been trailed — shipping 23 October, and the stock shrugged until Deepwater doubled its estimate of the Duo's share of fiscal 2027 iPhone revenue from 5%% to 10%%, sending it up 3.56%% and turning the position green. PLTR went the other way on a Citigroup downgrade, closing the week on its stop. Both were sell-side opinions rather than company news, which is worth noting: the book's two biggest moves this week came from analysts, not from the businesses.

4. Alphabet acquired a court. A US appeals court cleared 2,400–3,000-plus youth-addiction suits against Google, Meta, Snapchat and TikTok to proceed, and refused to delay the trial brought by 29 state attorneys general. That is materially larger than the FTC's YouTube probe this brief had been tracking, which remains unfiled after sixteen days. GOOG fell 2.09%% on the ruling and still finished the week as the book's steadiest name.

Oil stopped being a risk premium and became a supply number

WTI settled above $102 on Thursday and Brent reached $107.63, both through $100 for the first time since May, before Friday took WTI back to $99.05. The move was not a headline premium: Saudi Arabia reported production at its lowest level since 1990 after Houthi strikes on energy facilities including the 400,000 barrel-a-day Jazan refinery, and roughly ten commodity ships a day are crossing the Strait of Hormuz against a chokepoint that carries a fifth of world oil in peacetime. US petrol averaged $4.27 and diesel set a record.

The transmission into this book runs crude → CPI → the regime gate, and it worked all week. It also showed up somewhere more concrete: seven of the eight names in Phoenix's screener are now oil or marine shipping — DK, PBR, BP and PSX alongside BWLP, DAC and NMM. The war has stopped being a macro input and become what the screener returns. None of it is actionable while heat is over cap, and the screener has still reached nothing at its 20-bar horizon, so the verdict remains INSUFFICIENT.

Friday's 3.35%% fall in crude is the first thing to challenge that in two weeks. One down day from $102 is not a supply story ending.

Two central banks and an expiry, into a market that magnifies all three

FOMCFederal Reserve decision — a hike is 85.6% pricedWed2026-09-16
BOJBank of Japan decision — a hike is 97% pricedthis week2026-09-18
OPEXTriple witching — quarterly expiryFri2026-09-18

The Fed is the week. With a hike 85.6% priced the surprise is asymmetric: a hike is already in the price and a hold is not, so the larger move comes from the outcome nobody is positioned for — amplified by a dealer book still short gamma by $37.6B.

The Bank of Japan is the one that could hurt this book without any position being wrong. USDJPY is 153.57, -4.13% on the week and a fourth consecutive week of yen strength, with a hike 97% priced on a record ¥360tn of cross-border yen borrowing. Two central banks tightening in the same week, into negative gamma and a quarterly expiry, is the combination that turns an orderly repricing into a disorderly one.

Three things to check first on Monday. Whether PLTR's stop held on Friday; whether credit still refuses to worry — high yield has not moved in a week of 52-week highs in Treasuries, which is the most reassuring number anywhere in this brief; and whether heat is back under the cap, by a stop or by a decision.
